title: Grateful Dead Live at Saenger Performing Arts Center on 1982-09-09
source: Recording Info: Beyer M160 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-C90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Sony TC-K677ES) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/48k) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2.1 -> FLAC/16; Recorded by Frank Streeter; All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller

ai_review.summary: Lively audience tape captures a high‑energy 1982 Saenger show with a smoking Feel Like a Stranger and powerful Samson & Delilah, though the mix is uneven after the first few songs.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience (aud) source that shines during the opening half of the set, delivering clear, “dam good” sound on the first five tracks. The performance itself is high‑octane – reviewers rave about a rambunctious Feel Like a Stranger and a ferocious Samson & Delilah, plus a nostalgic West L.A. Fadeaway – but the later mix loses some clarity, prompting one listener to suggest ditching the soundboard altogether.

ai_rating.rationale: Two strong positive reviews (4 stars each) highlight energetic playing and good early‑set sound, while a single zero‑star review criticizes the setlist choice rather than performance; overall show quality is high but recording consistency is uneven.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early songs are crisp and clear; later portions become murkier, with some listeners preferring the audience tape over the soundboard. Overall lively ambience but inconsistent mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Unusual pairing of Samson & Delilah with Uncle John's (the “sandwich” oddity) noted, but overall the set maintains high energy and momentum.
